title: Generate Assertions Directly From the Response

Added: A "Generate from response" panel now lives right on the assertions table itself — expand it to see the response body (as a collapsible JSON tree), response headers, and the request headers actually sent, each with a one-click "+" to add an assertion row for that field, or "Generate all" to add every field in a section at once.
Assertions can now check request headers too (requestHeader.<Name>), not just response headers (header.<Name>) — available both as a Field-column autocomplete suggestion and from the new panel.
The panel is scoped to the exact request section the table belongs to in multi-request .void files, and to the table it's rendered on — never a different request's response or a different table.
Fixed: Generating from an unchanged response no longer creates duplicate assertion rows on repeat clicks — a field that already has an assertion is skipped (shown with a check instead of "+").
Generating a row no longer leaves a dangling empty row behind (e.g. the default table's leftover blank row is cleaned up as part of the same action).
Changed: The panel's sections (Request Headers / Response Headers / Body) are independently collapsible, and every toggle is keyboard-operable (Tab + Enter/Space), not click-only — Escape collapses the panel.

title: Docs: Skill Clarifies Assertion Table Rules and the contains Operator

Fixed: The bundled skill.md now clarifies that assertions-table is not currently enforced as singleton by the app (though one per section/request remains the recommended shape), and that the contains/not-contains operators only match string and array fields, not plain object fields — a limitation that was previously being reported as a bug when tested against an object field. Both are expected behavior, now documented as such.

Added: The Simple Assertions block now shows an inline "?" help tooltip in its header, matching the other request blocks
An "Open Documentation" item now appears in the Simple Assertions block's right-click block menu, opening the Voiden Blocks docs in your system browser

Improved: AI skill documentation updated with accurate operator names (hyphenated form), correct node schema, and expanded examples for in-editor guidance

Fixed: null and undefined values no longer incorrectly pass equals, contains, starts-with, ends-with, and regex operators — they now consistently fail
Numeric comparison operators (greater-than, less-than, greater-equal, less-equal) no longer return incorrect results when either value is non-numeric — NaN inputs now always fail
Response body is now parsed from JSON string before field access, fixing body.* assertions on JSON responses
Removed catch-all shim block that caused runtime bundle errors
Register assertions help entry in the command palette

description: Simple response assertions for Voiden REST API testing.
